subject: Service locus shift: temporary traffic reassignment & validation
messages:
From: Dan Cole <dan.cole@southgatemedia.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-11T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Increased 5xx/timeouts in US region — immediate help needed

Hi Ben,

We're seeing a spike of 502/504 responses and request timeouts from the Redwood hosted endpoints for our US tenants starting ~08:05 PST. Latency & 5xx count rose sharply, and a number of our customers' ingestion jobs failed. Sample: 08:06:12Z 502, 08:07:04Z 504, 08:08:31Z 502. Our oncall has throttled retries but the errors persist.

Can Redwood provide an immediate mitigation plan we can execute (we're prepared to update DNS/TLS bindings or point traffic temporarily if recommended). We need an ETA and a recommended short-term change that minimizes customer impact.

CC'ing our ops distribution: ops+oncall@southgatemedia.com

Thanks —
Dan
Director, Platform Engineering
Southgate Media

[Attachment: error-samples-08-11.txt]

Date: 2028-11-11T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Increased 5xx/timeouts in US region — mitigation plan

Ben / team,

Investigation notes (brief):
- Backend routing service in us-west-2 is seeing elevated connection churn due to a networking fabric degradation between two peering fabrics.
- Control plane healthy; serving nodes are reachable but some AZ-level egress is degrading, causing timeouts and downstream 502s.

Minimal safe mitigation we recommend for Southgate (customer-executed):
1) DNS override (temporary) — update their application DNS to prefer region eu (eu-west-1) for reads/write traffic to reduce latency to <150ms.
   - TTL: 60s for fast rollback.
   - Endpoint: api.eu.redwood.ai (CNAME) — see attached config snippet.
2) Client-side retry/backoff — reduce max parallelism to 6 for 5 minutes during switchover to avoid token storms.
3) KV-cache validation: run the included validation script to warm prefix caches in eu before shifting large traffic.

Attachments included: redwood-traffic-swivel-config.yaml (snippet), customer-kv-cache-validate.txt

Notes: We can also initiate a forced routing via our side (if they want us to flip). That requires an authenticated maintenance window and escalation to Dedicated Ops (we can do that, but customer-side change is faster).

--Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Dan Cole <dan.cole@southgatemedia.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-11T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Action plan: temporary service locus shift to EU (customer steps)

Dan —

Thanks for the quick report and the sample logs. We recommend the following immediate, customer-executed actions to minimize user impact while we work on the underlying fabric issue:

Planned short window (recommended): 11:15–11:30 PST (we will stand by during the swap)

1) Update DNS to prefer the EU endpoint (fast fallback):
   - Change CNAME for your Redwood API host to point to api.eu.redwood.ai
   - Set TTL=60s.
   - Example (we provide a config snippet in attached redwood-traffic-swivel-config.yaml).

2) Pre-warm EU prefix cache (important):
   - Run customer-kv-cache-validate.txt on a minimal client thread to populate common prefixes (run 2–3 quick requests over 2 minutes).

3) Reduce client concurrency during swap:
   - Limit parallel requests to 6 for the first 5 minutes after cutover.

If you'd rather have Redwood flip routing for you we can do it from our control plane; that requires an authenticated ops approval from your side and a 10-minute maintenance window. Customer-side DNS change is the fastest path.

We've attached a one-page runbook (runbook-service-locus-shift.pdf) and a short config snippet. Also linking the incident status page and the proposed post-incident call: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2028-11-11

Please confirm whether you want to proceed with the DNS plan at 11:15 PST or request Redwood to execute. We'll be on standby and will update you at +5 and +30 minutes after swap.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-service-locus-shift.pdf, redwood-traffic-swivel-config.yaml, customer-kv-cache-validate.txt
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Dan Cole <dan.cole@southgatemedia.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-11T15:42:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: mitigation complete & post-incident next steps

Dan —

Thanks — we saw the DNS change propagate at 11:17 PST and your traffic shifted to the EU endpoint as planned. Error rate dropped back to baseline by ~11:23 PST and latency recovered.

Immediate status:
- Incident mitigated for Southgate (traffic served from EU).
- Root cause: transient peering degradation in us-west-2 fabric; infra team is doing a deeper RCA.

Next steps:
- Redwood will produce a post-incident report (RCA + mitigation timeline) within 72 hours.
- Proposed postmortem call: 2028-11-13 at 10:00 PST — please confirm availability.
- We've uploaded the short runbook and intermediate logs to a shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleRunbook

If you want us to reverse traffic back to US when fabric repairs complete, reply with an approval and a target time window (we recommend keeping TTL at 60s for quick rollback).

Apologies for the disruption — we'll include recommended guardrails to prevent recurrence (traffic steering improvements and a faster-failover config) in the post-incident report.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: runbook-service-locus-shift.pdf]
